newsitem.title: UK: Microsoft aims to double UK internet users.
newsitem.headline: Microsoft aims to double UK internet users.

text.p: Microsoft Corp, the software giant which is challenging top Internet service providers with its fledging Microsoft Network, is using front-page advertisements in top British newspapers in efforts to at least double its UK subscriber base over the next year.
"The market still has so much room left to grow that we'd be foolish to not advertise," Taylor Collyer, marketing director for the Microsoft Network in the UK, told Reuters in a phone interview.

The ad campaign, which Collyer said cost somewhere between one million and 10 million pounds, is largely designed to promote awareness of the Microsoft Network, although it also contains a direct response element with a phone number listed in the ads.

The ad campaign, launched in early December, features teaser ads on newspaper front pages, which are linked to larger adverts on inside pages. "This way to the Internet," reads the headline on the teaser ad, which refers readers to an inside page in the newspaper.
On an inside page, the larger ad reads: "The New Microsoft Network. All that Internet stuff made easy. The revolutionary new MSN makes getting started on the Internet as easy as using your TV."

"A lot of people assume you have to know a lot of mumbo-jumbo to use the Internet," Collyer said. The ad campaign is emphasising that if you can use a TV or videocassette recorder, you can just as easily use the Internet.
The advert, which also offers a month's free trial of MSN, is running on a rotational basis in Britain's major daily newspapers.
"We'll be running it for a few more months, through the first quarter," Collyer said.
In conjunction with the newspaper ads, Microsoft has poster ads in certain stations of the London Underground.

"We have a second wave of the campaign, which is slated to run in the second quarter," Collyer said. The second quarter ad campaign is expected to cost at least as much as the current campaign, he said.
Microsoft, which has successfully used television ads in the U.S. to promote the Microsoft Network, is also considering doing some TV advertising as part of the second quarter campaign in Britain.

The Microsoft Network has two million subscribers worldwide, including 100,000 in the UK, with the average subscriber logging onto the Internet five to six hours a month. The U.S., which has the world's highest penetration of personal computers and greatest Internet usage, accounts the lion's share of subscribers, followed by Japan and the UK.
The UK has about 500,000 households with Internet access.

"We expect the (UK) market will increase by at least 50 percent in the coming year," Collyer said. "MSN expects to at least double in the next year in Britain, and MSN worldwide expects to at least double."

The number of new UK subscribers to MSN doubled over the normal weekly rate in the week between Christmas and New Year's. Collyer said the high rate likely reflects the number of people who received PCs as Christmas presents.
